'Has ISO 4217 code' is not functional: a currency can have several ISO 4217 codes at once. (edit)

notes: Removes a functional property that holds. The replace prompts ask whether a second value could hold, so the edit's answers are yes (balancing the topic's RBox yes/no against 0017, CRITERIA Rule 9); the delete asks the plain 'Does it follow ...?' around the original property. Functional property of the new relation has_iso_4217_code. It holds without exception: ISO 4217 assigns each currency exactly one alphabetic code (JPY, GBP, EUR, ...); codes change only when a currency is replaced or redenominated (TRL to TRY), never two at once, hence 'at the same time' in every prompt. Fund codes such as USN or CHE/CHW are separate entries for separate units, and the instances avoid those currencies. The second values (YEN, STG) are not the ISO codes of these currencies, so the original answers are right both by the property and in the world; a model that still excludes them after the edit uses world knowledge or the old property. Near: an ISIN identifies one security (ISO 6166), so the reference no differs from the replace's new answer yes. Locality references are the logical answers.
